sections.h2: Exterior failures we see around Fort White
body: Down by the Ichetucknee and through Three Rivers Estates, it is dampness that usually ruins a paint job. Green film forms on north walls, paint blisters where siding never fully dries, and soffits get soft under thick tree cover. On ranch properties, it fails from sun: chalky south walls, cracked caulk, and trim that has split and lost its coating. Exterior painting in Fort White, FL only lasts when the prep targets whatever is actually breaking the paint down, rather than simply rolling a new color over it.

Paint applied over damp wood will blister and peel, no matter the brand. On shaded homes, the crew lead takes moisture readings on suspect siding and trim during the walkthrough and again before priming. Boards that read wet and stay soft are replaced. During the wash, we apply a mildew treatment so the growth actually dies instead of just being blasted around the wall by plain water. Our soft washing in Fort White page explains the cleaning side.

bullets: Scrape off anything loose and scuff any shiny old paint
Swap rotten fascia or siding boards and reseat popped nails
Finish with two coats of acrylic, brushed in behind the sprayer
body: For Fort White lap siding and trim we specify 100% acrylic, a coating that lets trapped vapor out and flexes with temperature swings. Stucco showing hairline movement calls for an elastomeric instead, and entry doors plus porch rails get a waterborne urethane enamel. Your quote spells out the exact product line, which keeps the paint maker's warranty enforceable. Our article on what Florida's weather does to house paint goes deeper into why damp climates are so tough on coatings.

The best window is October through May. Shaded walls dry slowly after a storm, so crews may start on the sunny sides in the morning and move to the shaded ones once they are dry. July and August jobs begin around sunrise, with the crew lead checking the dew point and storm radar throughout the day. Most Fort White houses take three to seven working days of painting, with wash and dry days added in front. Planning a new look? Book a Fort White color consultation first so colors are settled before we lock in dates. The complete process is laid out on our exterior painting page, and everything else we do in town is on the Fort White overview.

faqs.q: Why does paint peel faster on my shaded Fort White home?
faqs.a: Under the trees, siding takes much longer to dry after rain, which feeds mildew and lets water work in behind the paint. Killing growth, checking moisture, and replacing wet wood before painting addresses the cause.

faqs.q: When is the best time to paint an exterior in Fort White?
faqs.a: Aim for the months from October to May. A summer exterior is doable, but each day starts at dawn and hinges on the dew point and what the radar shows.

faqs.q: Do you paint commercial buildings on Main Street?
faqs.a: Yes. For Main Street shops we can paint outside your open hours, including evenings and weekends if that is what keeps the doors open.

faqs.q: What warranty comes with an exterior repaint?
faqs.a: Fort White exteriors carry our workmanship warranty in writing for up to 10 years, separate from and added to the coating manufacturer's warranty.
